The paper distinguishes bounded, differentiable tau from nonsmooth perturbations such as chopping; in the nonsmooth case it replaces cancellation conditions by componentwise absolute-value products that must vanish. [PDF p. 6; anchor: paragraphs immediately preceding Section 3.1]

Consistency through order two requires tilde b e=1 and tilde b tilde c=1/2. For non-well-behaved tau, perturbation order through m=2 requires |b^epsilon||e|=0 and |tilde b||c^epsilon|=0. [PDF p. 7; anchor: consistency conditions and conditions (3.4a)-(3.4b)]

For well-behaved tau, perturbation order through m=2 requires b^epsilon e=0, b^epsilon tilde c=0, tilde b c^epsilon=0, and b^epsilon c^epsilon=0, with the last condition listed under n>=2. [PDF p. 8; anchor: conditions (3.5a)-(3.5c)]

It explicitly records b^epsilon tilde c=0 and tilde b c^epsilon=0. [PDF p. 11; anchor: corrected method (4.1a)-(4.1c), displayed Butcher arrays, and the two unnumbered cancellation identities]

binders: Let Delta t be the time step, u^n the current state, F the high-precision operator, F^epsilon its low-precision approximation, and epsilon the perturbation scale. [PDF p. 3; anchor: equations (2.3)-(2.4b)]

For the selected coefficient certificate, instantiate the additive Runge-Kutta framework with two stages corresponding to y_[0]^(1) and y_[1]^(1). [PDF p. 11; anchor: equations (4.1a)-(4.1c) and displayed arrays]

Let e denote the length-two all-ones vector as inherited from the standard Runge-Kutta contractions appearing in the consistency conditions. [PDF p. 7; anchor: consistency conditions through order two]
hypotheses: The perturbation model is F^epsilon(y)-F(y)=O(epsilon), with tau(y)=(F(y)-F^epsilon(y))/epsilon. [PDF pp. 3-4; anchors: equation (2.3) and paragraph following equations (3.1a)-(3.1b)]
The selected method uses the low-precision operator only in the implicit initial stage and high-precision F in the correction and final update. [PDF p. 11; anchor: equations (4.1a)-(4.1c)]

The smooth branch assumes tau is well behaved so corresponding perturbation terms may cancel; the nonsmooth branch does not permit that cancellation and imposes absolute-value conditions. [PDF pp. 6-8; anchors: paragraphs preceding Section 3.1 and Sections 3.1.1-3.1.2]

Stability is required only for the paper's subsequent global-error expectation, not for the exact coefficient identities. [PDF pp. 2 and 11; anchors: stability discussion in Section 1 and paragraph below the cancellation identities]
conclusions: The exact corrected coefficients are A=[[0,0],[1/2,0]], c=[0,1/2], b=[0,1], A^epsilon=[[1/2,0],[0,0]], c^epsilon=[1/2,0], and b^epsilon=[0,0]. [PDF p. 11; anchor: displayed Butcher arrays below (4.1a)-(4.1c)]
Their exact sums are tilde A=A+A^epsilon=[[1/2,0],[1/2,0]], tilde c=c+c^epsilon=[1/2,1/2], and tilde b=b+b^epsilon=[0,1]. [PDF p. 11; anchor: displayed combined arrays]

Substitution gives the complete order-two consistency certificate tilde b e=1 and tilde b tilde c=1/2. [PDF pp. 7 and 11; anchors: consistency conditions through order two and displayed combined arrays]

For well-behaved tau, substitution gives b^epsilon e=0, b^epsilon tilde c=0, tilde b c^epsilon=0, and b^epsilon c^epsilon=0, satisfying every listed smooth perturbation condition through m=2. [PDF pp. 8 and 11; anchors: conditions (3.5a)-(3.5c), displayed arrays, and unnumbered identities]

For non-well-behaved tau, substitution gives |b^epsilon||e|=0 and |tilde b||c^epsilon|=0, satisfying every listed nonsmooth perturbation condition through m=2. [PDF pp. 7 and 11; anchors: conditions (3.4a)-(3.4b) and displayed arrays]

The paper explicitly highlights b^epsilon tilde c=0 and tilde b c^epsilon=0 and states that these identities eliminate the O(epsilon Delta t^2) term. [PDF p. 11; anchor: two unnumbered identities and the sentence immediately below]
definitions_and_conventions: tau(u)=(F(u)-F^epsilon(u))/epsilon, so equivalently F^epsilon=F-epsilon tau wherever the definition is used algebraically. [PDF p. 3; anchor: equation (2.3)]
The additive coefficients attached to F and F^epsilon are respectively A,b and A^epsilon,b^epsilon; tilde A=A+A^epsilon and tilde b=b+b^epsilon. [PDF pp. 4-5; anchors: equations (3.1a)-(3.2b)]
For the displayed corrected method, tilde c=c+c^epsilon is explicitly formed alongside tilde A and tilde b. [PDF p. 11; anchor: displayed combined arrays]

The bars in the nonsmooth conditions denote componentwise absolute values whose products are required to vanish, rather than a state-space norm. [PDF pp. 6-7; anchors: paragraph preceding Section 3.1 and conditions (3.4a)-(3.4b)]

The displayed two-stage arrays correspond to one correction, identified in the accompanying prose as p=2. [PDF p. 11; anchor: numerical-results paragraph below (4.1)]

statement.algorithm_linkage: Equation (4.1a) implicitly computes y_[0]^(1)=u^n+(Delta t/2)F^epsilon(y_[0]^(1)); equation (4.1b) computes the explicit high-precision correction y_[1]^(1)=u^n+(Delta t/2)F(y_[0]^(1)); and for the one-correction case p=2, equation (4.1c) updates u^(n+1)=u^n+Delta t F(y_[1]^(1)). The displayed arrays encode exactly this p=2 variant. [PDF p. 11; anchor: equations (4.1a)-(4.1c), displayed arrays, and p=2 description]
numerical_model: F is treated as the accurate or high-precision evaluation and F^epsilon as an approximation differing from it by O(epsilon). [PDF pp. 3-4; anchors: equations (2.3)-(2.4b) and paragraph following (3.1b)]

Mixed-precision chopping is given as a motivating nonsmooth realization, for which F^epsilon=Chop(F) can be bounded but non-Lipschitz and derivatives of tau may fail to exist. [PDF p. 6; anchor: paragraph immediately preceding Section 3.1]

The selected certificate specifies no IEEE format, rounding direction, unit roundoff formula, or operation-by-operation rounding semantics beyond the abstract F^epsilon perturbation model. [PDF pp. 3-4 and 11; anchors: equation (2.3), additive framework (3.1), and corrected method (4.1)]
error_notions: The paper separates one-step error into scheme error E_sch and perturbation error E_per. [PDF p. 5; anchor: equation (3.3) and following paragraph]

The exact selected claim is coefficient cancellation of the O(epsilon Delta t^2) perturbation term, not an equality between computed and exact trajectories. [PDF p. 11; anchor: two unnumbered identities and following sentence]

The global expression Error=O(Delta t^2)+O(epsilon Delta t^2) is stated only as an expectation conditional on stability under the low-precision perturbation. [PDF p. 11; anchor: paragraph immediately below the cancellation identities]
norms: No norm on states, operators, local errors, or global errors is specified in the selected result. [PDF pp. 5 and 11; anchors: equation (3.3) error discussion and corrected-method cancellation paragraph]

contract_plain_english: For the one-correction implicit-midpoint method, perform the initial implicit stage with F^epsilon, perform the correction and final evaluation with F, and use exactly the two-stage arrays printed on PDF page 11. [PDF p. 11; anchor: equations (4.1a)-(4.1c) and displayed arrays] Those arrays give tilde b e=1 and tilde b tilde c=1/2, so the underlying method is exactly consistent through order two. [PDF pp. 7 and 11; anchors: consistency conditions and displayed combined arrays] They also satisfy every smooth and nonsmooth perturbation condition listed through m=2; in particular, the paper explicitly records b^epsilon tilde c=0 and tilde b c^epsilon=0, eliminating the O(epsilon Delta t^2) term. [PDF pp. 7-8 and 11; anchors: conditions (3.4a)-(3.5c) and unnumbered cancellation identities] The later global expression O(Delta t^2)+O(epsilon Delta t^2) is only surrounding, stability-conditional asymptotic context and is not the exact selected certificate. [PDF p. 11; anchor: paragraph below the cancellation identities]
